reason: Tech stack (Tauri 2 / React 18 / Zustand 5 / Vite 6) and key conventions (@/ alias, named exports, invoke() pattern) — anchors all frontend edits.
WebviewWindow creation, label conventions, ACL permission contract for @tauri-apps/api/webview-window, multi-window lifecycle — directly governs the new ToolWindowManager.
Zustand store conventions (granular selectors, no bare useStore, action/selector split) — new toolWindowStore must follow these.
Component patterns + props composition + no default exports — governs any UI added (e.g. error fallback when a tool window fails to load).
Where new files go (services/plugin-host vs store vs components) — keeps toolWindowStore + adapter in the right layer.
No `any`, named exports, useEffect cleanup, file-size limits, review checklist — applies to all new TS/TSX.
Strict TS, type narrowing with `unknown` at boundaries — RPC request/response shape must be typed, not any-cast.
Plugin-host package conventions — confirms where registerPluginTools adapter sits in the contribution surface.
Frontend↔Rust boundary discipline — the /rpc POST handler touches Rust (plugin_commands.rs) + JS (editorStore); this guide governs the contract between layers.
Pre-Modification Rule: search before changing. rpcBridge.ts already has isPathInScope + permission checks — reuse, don't reimplement.
uTools plugin model reference (manifest, full-window tool, isolation) — the UX target this task is matching.
